subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the order of operations (BIDMAS), which operation is carried out first?
questions.explain: BIDMAS states that Brackets are evaluated before indices, division, multiplication, addition and subtraction.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explain: 29 has exactly two factors, 1 and itself, whereas 51 = 3 x 17, 39 = 3 x 13 and 1 is not prime.

questions.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 36?
questions.explain: The largest number that divides exactly into both 24 and 36 is 12.

questions.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
questions.explain: 24 is the smallest number that is a multiple of both 6 and 8.

questions.q: Calculate -6 x -4.
questions.explain: A negative multiplied by a negative gives a positive result, so -6 x -4 = 24.

questions.q: What is a fraction whose numerator is larger than its denominator called?
questions.explain: An improper (top-heavy) fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its denominator.

questions.q: Work out 3/4 + 1/8.
questions.explain: Writing 3/4 as 6/8 gives 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.q: Work out 2/3 x 3/5, giving your answer in its simplest form.
questions.explain: Multiplying gives 6/15, which simplifies to 2/5.

questions.q: What is 10% written as a decimal?
questions.explain: 10% means 10 out of 100, which equals 0.1.

questions.q: Find 25% of 80.
questions.explain: 25% is one quarter, and one quarter of 80 is 20.

questions.q: A jacket costs £40. In a sale it is reduced by 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explain: A 15% reduction leaves 85%, and 0.85 x £40 = £34.

questions.q: What is the value of the square root of 64?
questions.explain: 8 x 8 = 64, so the square root of 64 is 8.

questions.q: What is 5 cubed (5³)?
Using the laws of indices, simplify 2³ x 2⁴.
questions.explain: When multiplying powers of the same base you add the indices, so 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.q: In standard form written as a x 10ⁿ, what is the allowed range for the value of a?
questions.explain: In standard form the number a must be at least 1 but less than 10.

questions.q: Write 34,000 in standard form.
Round 3.14159 to 2 decimal places.
questions.explain: The third decimal digit is 1, which rounds down, leaving 3.14.

questions.q: Round 4567 to 2 significant figures.
questions.explain: The first two significant figures are 4 and 5; the next digit is 6, so it rounds up to 4600.

questions.q: Estimate the value of 19.6 x 4.1 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
questions.explain: Rounding gives 20 x 4 = 80.

questions.q: A length is measured as 12 cm to the nearest centimetre. What are its lower and upper bounds?
questions.explain: To the nearest cm, the true value lies within half a unit of 12, giving bounds of 11.5 cm and 12.5 cm.
